| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

input.content:
## Summary

These are the foundation docs that every coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity) follows for Locke. This PR contains docs only, no app code.

- **`AGENTS.md`**: the rulebook for all four harnesses.
  - Product summary, plus trust principles written as coding rules: the Safe Route rule, missing evidence never counts as fraud, no numeric trust score, the outcome is decided by code, the verifier can only downgrade, and no accusatory language.
  - Architecture with a mermaid diagram, repo layout and file ownership, version pins, env var names, and coding and testing rules.
  - neatlogs tracing and Entire checkpoint rules, git and PR conventions, and a definition of done.
  - Orchestrator dispatch: which harness owns which files, task-sizing limits, and how shared types are handed off.
  - Baseline UI and motion rules for harnesses without design skills. `DESIGN.md` is required reading for UI work.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: imports `AGENTS.md`, then says when to use each Claude Code skill.
- **`docs/SPEC.md`**: the full product spec.
  - The 7 investigation questions mapped to 6 Dossier dimensions, each with exact status codes.
  - 4 outcomes decided by fixed rules (R1–R4), plus the verifier and the guard checks G1–G6.
  - Contracts for each tool (Crustdata, the 5 ATS APIs, RDAP, DNS over HTTPS, an SSRF-safe fetch, and the OpenRouter web plugin), the data model, API routes, and the SSE event protocol.
  - Pages, design requirements (`DESIGN.md` is the source of truth for tokens), accessibility, privacy, a 25-case eval design and its metrics, the hackathon evidence plan, the demo beat sheet, the business model, and risks.
- **`docs/PLAN.md`**: a time-boxed plan from M0 to M5.
  - 28 tasks of 2–4h spread across the 4 harnesses. Each lists dependencies, owned files, acceptance criteria and skills.
  - Waves that can run in parallel, and the human-only tasks H1–H9.
  - locke-5 (Codex scaffold and the first-trace gate) and locke-6 (Antigravity brand and `DESIGN.md`) are recorded as already dispatched.
- **`hackathon.md`**: the neatHack build log, in the format of the neatlogs hackathon skill.
- **`.env.example`**: env var names only.

## Test plan

- [x] The `AGENTS.md` mermaid diagram renders with `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` 11.
- [x] Pins checked against the npm registry: `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-postgres@0.1.3` is the last line whose peer range includes `@langchain/core` <0.4. `@langchain/langgraph@0.4.10` and `@langchain/openai@0.6.17` peer on core 0.3.
- [x] The OpenRouter web plugin, the Crustdata `/company/identify` endpoint, and the format of the neatlogs hackathon skill were checked against their live docs.
- [x] File lengths: `AGENTS.md` is 308 lines (limit ~350) and `CLAUDE.md` is 90 (limit ~150).
- [ ] Owners of locke-5 and locke-6 confirm their file ownership matches `AGENTS.md` §4 and §13.

## Notes and risks

- The Entire CLI was not installed when these commits were made, so they have no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Human task H2 installs Entire before the scaffold merges.
- neatlogs 1.1.28 is now the latest on npm. The docs keep the researched 1.1.21 pin and only change it if the first-trace gate fails.
- Workable's public jobs endpoint is unofficial. Task T07 checks it.

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

The reviewer was right: the spec had the channel investigator comparing a supplied link with itself, so a direct attacker link would come back as `same`. I've fixed it in `docs/SPEC.md` (commit `7dd24d9`), pushed it to PR #2, replied on the thread and resolved it. The PR is still not merged.

- **Channel investigator:** checks both the starting and final host of the supplied link. Each is compared against the employer's official domain plus the ATS job boards linked from it, and the worse result of the two counts.
- **New rule (§6.4):** the comparison is always against those established employer channels. A recruiter-supplied URL, a redirect step, or a sender's domain can never be treated as the official domain. If no employer channel was established, the link is "could not check" and the recruiter is "could not verify". The spec now also calls for a unit test that an unrelated supplied link never comes back as matching the employer.
- **Guard G4:** now applies to "matches employer channel" as well as "does not match", and a match must cite evidence from the employer's own site or a linked ATS board.
- **Recruiter investigator:** compares the sender's domain against the official domain the same way.

I sent the orchestrator a checkpoint report.

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

content.text:
The second review comment was also right, and it's fixed in commit `af9e011`, pushed to PR #2. I replied on the thread, resolved it, and sent the orchestrator a checkpoint report; the PR is still not merged.

The problem was ordering. The guard ran before the resolver, but only the resolver picked the Safe Route. So the guard's Safe Route check (G3) had no route to validate. The outcome rule for "Verified route available" (R2) also never saw a confirmed route, so fully confirmed cases would miss that outcome.

The new order:
- **Guard node:** applies G1, G2, G4 and G6 to the findings, then runs `selectSafeRoute`, then G3 validates the chosen route. It writes the result as the `safe_route` finding.
- **Resolver:** runs `decideOutcome` on those checked findings, so R2 now sees a confirmed route. It never re-selects or changes the route. The language check (G5) stays here because it checks the generated text.

I also updated the `AGENTS.md` diagram (it still renders) and added to task T12's acceptance criteria a test of this order, including a fully confirmed case that ends in "Verified route available".

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

content.content:
- **Acceptance:** The SPEC §9 routes with zod validation, 404/409/429 paths tested, and redaction
  applied before insert. SSE emits `StreamEvent`s in `seq` order. On abort: the graph is aborted, the
  run is marked `cancelled`, and `flush()` runs in `finally`. `PostgresSaver.setup()` is in
  `db:setup`. `LOCKE_CHECKPOINTER=memory|postgres`. The screenshot is transcribed via a traced call
  and never persisted (a test asserts the DB row and checkpoint contain no base64).
- **Skills:** `superpowers:test-driven-development`, `langgraph-persistence`, `security-review`.

### T14 Stream integration, fault-injected recovery, fixture recording (Claude Code, 3h, W5)
8. **Candidate control.** Locke never sends email, applies, or contacts anyone. It drafts and the
   user decides.
9. **Privacy by default.** Raw user input is redacted (`redactPii`) before it enters graph state,
   tracing, or the database. Screenshots are never stored.
10. **No discriminatory inference.** Never use names, nationality, language, or protected traits as
## Known limitations and next steps
- Planned limitations for V1: no accounts; no multi-message case threads; Locke never sends email;
  personal names are not redacted (only contact details, IDs, and financial numbers are); screenshot
  content is visible in the transcription trace span.
- Next steps: see `docs/PLAN.md`, starting with M0.

git diff --stat && git commit -qam "fix(spec): keep raw screenshots out of neatlogs traces

The spec traced the screenshot vision call with the shared handler,
which would have stored the unredacted image in neatlogs. That call now
runs without the handler and is traced through a manual
screenshot:transcribe span that records an image placeholder, the
redacted transcription, the model slug and token usage. Tests assert
that no base64 reaches the span, the DB or the checkpoint. AGENTS.md
documents this as the one exception to the handler rule, and PLAN T13
and hackathon.md are updated to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q 2>&1 | tail -2; git log --oneline -1; git status -sb | head -1

The reviewer was right: the spec traced the screenshot transcription call with the normal neatlogs handler, so the unredacted image would have been stored in neatlogs. The fix is in commit `a9e6d56`, pushed to PR #2; I replied on the thread, resolved it, and sent the orchestrator a checkpoint report. The PR is still not merged.

- **New rule (SPEC §14):** the screenshot vision call is now the only LLM call made without the neatlogs handler. A manual traced step wraps it and records only:
  - a placeholder in place of the image (`[omitted: <mime>, <KB> KB]`)
  - the redacted transcription
  - the model name and token usage

  The image stays in memory for that one call and is never put in graph state, a checkpoint, the database, or a trace.
- **neatlogs masking:** if the neatlogs SDK turns out to support masking a span's input, it can replace the manual wrapper. That only happens after reading a trace back confirms no image data reached neatlogs.
- **Required tests:** the vision call is built without the handler, and no image data or unredacted personal data reaches the span, the database, or the checkpoint.
- **Other docs updated to match:** `AGENTS.md` (the privacy rule now says screenshots are never traced raw, and the tracing rules list this as the one exception), task T13 in the plan, risk R7, and the limitations in `hackathon.md`.

The "crop out personal details" notice stays in the UI, because OpenRouter and the model provider still receive the image.

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

The reviewer was right, and the fix is in commit `f90eb46`, pushed to PR #2; I replied on the thread, resolved it, and sent the orchestrator a checkpoint report. The PR is still not merged.

`requests=none_detected` was marked positive, but the requests investigator only reads the recruiter's own message, so it could never cite the independent evidence that guard G1 requires.

It is now neutral, with the label "No payment or sensitive-data requests in what you shared". Not finding a request in the recruiter's text is an observation, not a verification, so G1 no longer applies to it and the downgrade rules need no path from it. The outcome rules never depended on it being positive, so they are unchanged.

A plugin hook that blocks `--no-verify` misfired on my first commit command, even though the command didn't use that flag. I committed with a message file instead and skipped no git hooks.

## [stale] Obsidian Brain [NoteType.PROJECT] 
## Purpose

Local-first memory system for coding agents. Stores structured notes as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `projects/<project>/`. Human-readable in Obsidian, diff-friendly in Git, no running app server required.

## Key Decisions

- **File-as-truth**: No database -- Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are the canonical store. SQLite and vector DBs were rejected to keep the vault portable and inspectable.
- **CLI-first, MCP second**: All functionality lives in the `vault-memory` CLI; the MCP server is a thin FastMCP wrapper that shells out to the CLI so both surfaces stay in sync.
- **BM25 + graph expansion**: Search uses rank-bm25 with type-priority and recency boosts; `_graph_index.json` expands neighbors for richer context without requiring a running graph DB.
- **Token-budgeted context packs**: `context-pack` assembles home > summary > BM25 results > recent sessions in priority order, truncating to fit the token budget (default 2500).
- **Hooks over always-on server**: Session start/end are Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit / Stop) rather than a persistent daemon, keeping the system lightweight.
- **Dropped graphify dependency**: Graph index is built from frontmatter `related` fields only; the external graphify package was removed to eliminate subprocess hangs.

## Architecture

Module stack (vault_memory/):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| config.py | VaultConfig dataclass; reads .vault-config.json |
| schema.py | NoteType enum and NoteMeta dataclass |
| store.py | Read/write .md files with frontmatter + file lock |
| search.py | BM25 search with type-priority and recency boost |
| graph.py | Loads _graph_index.json, expands neighbors |
| context_pack.py | Token-budgeted pack: home > summary > BM25 > sessions |
| session.py | record_session() and write_summary() |
| links.py | Bidirectional linking + upsert_note() |
| git.py | auto_commit() after writes; recent_changes() |
| cli.py | Click CLI; all commands emit JSON |

Entry points:
- vault-memory: vault_memory.cli:main
- vault-memory-mcp: mcp_server.server:main (FastMCP)

Hooks (hooks/):
- session_start.py -- UserPromptSubmit: injects context-pack before every prompt
- session_end.py -- Stop: writes session note from claudeSummary
- compact_hook.py -- PostCompact: writes rich compaction summary

## Open Questions

- Should the MCP server import vault_memory directly (faster, no subprocess) rather than shelling out to the CLI?
- Token budget of 2500 may be too small for complex projects -- should it be dynamically sized based on context window?
- Graph index rebuild strategy: currently manual via graphify_runner.py; could auto-rebuild on every upsert for small vaults.

lines: `lib/agent/run.ts` and runs against a stub iterable until T11 merges.
- **Owns:** `app/api/**`, `lib/db/**` (`client.ts`, `cases.ts`, `schema.sql`), `lib/server/sse.ts`
(`AsyncIterable<StreamEvent>` → SSE `Response`), `lib/server/rate-limit.ts`, `scripts/db-setup.ts`.
-- **Acceptance:** The SPEC §9 routes with zod validation, 404/409/429 paths tested, and redaction
+- **Acceptance:** The SPEC §9 routes with zod validation, 404/409/422/429 paths tested (including a screenshot-only case), and redaction
applied before insert. SSE emits `StreamEvent`s in `seq` order. On abort: the graph is aborted, the
run is marked `cancelled`, and `flush()` runs in `finally`. `PostgresSaver.setup()` is in
`db:setup`. `LOCKE_CHECKPOINTER=memory|postgres`. The screenshot vision call runs **without**
| Route | Body / params | Response |
-| `POST /api/cases` | `{ text?: string ≤ 20000, url?: url }` (at least one) | `201 { id }`. Text is redacted before storage. 10 per hour per IP. |

+| `POST /api/cases` | `{ text?: string ≤ 20000, url?: url, hasScreenshot?: boolean }` (at least one of `text`, `url`, or `hasScreenshot: true`) | `201 { id }`. Text is redacted before storage. `hasScreenshot` is stored as `input.hadScreenshot`. The image itself is **not** sent here (see `/run`). 10 per hour per IP. |
| `GET /api/cases/[id]` | n/a | `200 Case` or `404` |

-| `POST /api/cases/[id]/run` | `{ image?: { mime: "image/png"\|"image/jpeg"\|"image/webp", base64 ≤ 4 MB } }` | `200 text/event-stream`. `409` if a run is active or a Dossier exists. The image is transcribed by the worker model (vision), and the transcription is redacted and appended to the input. **The image is never put in graph state, the checkpointer, the DB, or any trace** (see §14 for how the call is traced without it). |

+| `POST /api/cases/[id]/run` | `{ image?: { mime: "image/png"\|"image/jpeg"\|"image/webp", base64 ≤ 4 MB } }` | `200 text/event-stream`. `409` if a run is active or a Dossier exists. `422 { code: "screenshot_required" }` if the case has no text and no URL and no image was sent. The image is transcribed by the worker model (vision), and the transcription is redacted and appended to the input. **The image is never put in graph state, the checkpointer, the DB, or any trace** (see §14 for how the call is traced without it). |
| `POST /api/cases/[id]/resume` | `{ answer: string ≤ 500 } \| { skip: true }` | `200 text/event-stream` continuing the thread via `Command({ resume })`. `409` if the case is not `needs_input`. |
The client holds a pending screenshot in memory (`lib/client/pending-upload.ts`) between
-`/investigate` and `/case/[id]`. If the page reloads, the screenshot is gone and the run proceeds
-without it.
+`/investigate` and `/case/[id]`. If the page reloads, the screenshot is gone. A case that also has
+text or a URL proceeds without it. A **screenshot-only** case gets `422 screenshot_required` from
+`/run`, and the case page shows a re-upload drop zone that retries `/run` with the image.

**SSE format:** `event: <type>
data: <json>

`. Every event has `{ seq, ts, runId }` and is a
member of the `StreamEvent` discriminated union in `lib/types/events.ts`:

input.content:
fix(spec): allow creating a case from a screenshot alone

POST /api/cases required text or a URL, but the image is only sent to
/run once a case ID exists, so a screenshot-only submission had no valid
first request. Creation now also accepts hasScreenshot: true, stored as
input.hadScreenshot. /run returns 422 screenshot_required when a
screenshot-only case arrives without its image (for example after a
reload), and the case page offers a re-upload. PLAN T09, T13 and T16 are
updated to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
